record.set: England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975 (FamilySearch index), confirmed on FindMyPast and FamilySearch independently

lede: This archive has spent weeks looking for Hannah Saniger's baptism, and on two separate days concluded it was missing from every index money could buy. It is not missing. It is spelled SANIGOR, and that is one of the very few spellings this site's own alias list did not carry.
why: The search index here knows eleven forms of this surname — Sainger, Sanigar, Sanigaer, Sinager, Sinneger, Sinnegar, Sinegar, Synegar, Synager, Singer. It did not know Sanigor. Neither did the variant matching on the subscription site, which returned her marriage and nothing else however the query was phrased. One vowel.

siblings.head: And with it, the whole family
siblings.note: John Saniger's children, all baptised at Berkeley, all naming him as father:
rows: almost certainly the Thomas Sinegar who lived a mile from her in Bristol

year.head: One thing does not fit, and it is the year.
year.body: The family tree gives Hannah's birth as 23 July 1805. This baptism is 18 August 1804 — eleven months earlier. There is no second Hannah baptised to John Saniger at Berkeley, and no burial for a Hannah between the two dates, so the ordinary reading is that the tree's day and month were carried from somewhere reliable and the year slipped by one. The alternative — two daughters of the same name, the first dying unrecorded — is possible and has no evidence at all.
year.chip: her baptism, very probably; the year unresolved

lydia.head: Her mother is named, and the name is not evidenced.
lydia.body: FamilySearch's shared tree gives John Saniger a wife LYDIA JONES, 1770–1851, married at Berkeley in 1797. That would name the seventy-year-old Lyddya Sinegar living in Hannah's house in 1841 and settle the oldest small mystery on this site.
lydia.but: It is not sourced. John Saniger's profile there carries fourteen sources and every one of them is a baptism — his own and his children's. No marriage record is attached, and no record anywhere in this archive gives Lydia a surname. JONES is somebody's assertion until a Berkeley marriage register says otherwise.
lydia.chip: a name to test, not a fact
lydia.tree: AND THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN DATA HOLDS FOUR MORE FIELDS THAT THIS PAGE NEVER MENTIONED: Lydia Jones born 13 MARCH 1770 AT WOTTON-UNDER-EDGE, Gloucestershire; parents WILLIAM JONES and SARAH; died 7 JULY 1851 AT BERKELEY. Every one of those is testable and none has been tested. A death at Berkeley in July 1851 is inside civil registration and should sit in the September quarter of the GRO index for the Thornbury district. A baptism at Wotton-under-Edge in March 1770 to William and Sarah Jones is an ordinary register lookup. A week was spent deciding the surname was unevidenced without trying either.

thomas: It also closes the Thomas Sinegar question. He and Hannah are both baptised at Berkeley to John Saniger — she in 1804, he on 3 July 1808 — and he spent his life in the Bristol parish next to hers, naming a daughter Lydia, a daughter Hannah, and two sons John.
ancestry: Asked to look on Ancestry, which holds the Gloucestershire registers FindMyPast does not. It is not signed in on this machine and I will not enter anyone's password, so it was not used. FamilySearch was signed in, is free, and had the record.

probate.head: And there is no will to ask.
probate.body: A will names children, and that is the shortest route from John Saniger of Berkeley to his daughter Hannah. The Gloucestershire probate index for the right period — Gloucestershire Wills & Administrations 1801-1858, the Consistory Court of Gloucester, 14,195 entries — was read this fortnight under every opening this surname takes. It holds exactly TWO of them.
rows: ABRAHAM SYNEGAR, CARDMAKER, of DURSLEY — administration, 1813/8
JOHN SANIGAR, CARPENTER, of OLDBURY-ON-SEVERN, Thornbury — will, 1822/194
probate.means: Neither is Berkeley. The John Sanigar of 1822 is the Thornbury outlier this archive already knew about, ten miles down the Vale and in the wrong parish; a cardmaker at Dursley makes the combs that card wool, which is the Stroudwater trade the reconstitution found. THERE IS NO SANIGER OF BERKELEY IN THE GLOUCESTERSHIRE PROBATE INDEX AT ALL, which means John Saniger left no proved will and no administration in the diocesan court — the ordinary outcome for a man with nothing much to leave, and a closed door rather than an unopened one.
probate.how: Searched with wildcards rather than spellings — SAN*, SIN*, SYN* and SWA* return every form the name takes and 27 surrounding families besides, so no spelling can hide inside this result the way SANIGOR hid a baptism. Control: SMITH in the same index returns 277.
probate.chip: searched, empty, and the coverage established

fmp.head: All one hundred and fifty-eight, read
fmp.lede: FindMyPast's **England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975** carries a column this archive has never had from an index: **the father's first name**. For SANIGER it holds **158 baptisms**, and **156 of them name a father**. All eight pages have now been read in baptism-year order, 1571 to 1909. **115 of the 158 are Berkeley** — the rest are Bristol (9), Thornbury (7), Stone and Tidenham (4 each), Dursley and St Botolph Aldgate (3 each), King's Stanley and Stonehouse (2 each), and one apiece at Frampton on Severn, Slimbridge, North Nibley, Wheatenhurst and Newent. Two strays sit far outside all of it, both in 1688: Nether Whitacre in Warwickshire and Stoke Prior in Worcestershire.
rows: already on this page — see the correction below
fmp.john: The four SANIGER children of John Saniger of Berkeley — **Ann 1798, William 1801, John 1803, Thomas 1808** — now stand with **their father named in the index**, not asserted by a tree. With **Hannah Sanigor, 18 August 1804**, that is the complete set of five, and every one of them names JNO or JOHN. This is the deepest line in the archive and until this week the only thing holding the sibling group together was other people's trees.
fmp.fix: Yesterday this section said **“Ann has never had a baptism”** and presented her 1798 entry as a new find. She had been on this page since 13 September, four blocks above, in the sibling table, as *Ann Sanigar 1798*. I read one page of an index, matched a name against what the tree asserts, and did not read the page I was writing on. It is the same entry under a different vowel. Recorded as own error 33.
fmp.hannahHead: The null under SANIGER is now a real null
fmp.hannah: There is **no Hannah in the set between 1777 and 1817** under this spelling. The only two are Berkeley 1746, father Thomas, and Berkeley 1772, father William — the second entered twice. That is no longer a guess about an index: every one of the 158 has been read. **She is there under SANIGOR**, which is why she was found on 13 September and not before, and this pass is the coverage that makes the SANIGER absence worth stating.
fmp.gapHead: And what the set is not
fmp.gap: **Thirty-three of the 158 are duplicates** — 125 distinct name-year-place combinations, so one entry in five is the same child indexed twice, sometimes four times: Mary, daughter of Samuell, appears four times in 1688, and Sarah, daughter of William, four times at Bristol in 1839. The Berkeley run also has holes, and they are the holes of a register rather than of a family: **1632 to 1676, forty-four years with nothing**, then 1749–1769, 1777–1786, 1808–1817 and 1826–1835. Counting this surname's presence by decade from this set alone would be counting the survival of paper.
fmp.awreHead: It also closes something this archive got wrong
fmp.awre: Own error 32 was a Forest-of-Dean branch of this family that I invented and then built on. Here is a third independent test of it: **158 baptisms across 268 years contain no Awre, no Blakeney, and nothing anywhere west of the Severn.** Bigland said so, Rudder said so, the 1608 muster said so, and now the parish registers say so.

lydiaTested.head: Her mother, tested
lydiaTested.lede: The block above was written on 13 September and ended by saying that four fields about Lydia were «testable and none has been tested». All four have now been tested, in one afternoon, on the subscription this archive already had. **Two are confirmed from record, one is wrong, and one has nothing behind it.**
rows: **LYDIA SANIGAR**, death registered in the **September quarter of 1851, Thornbury district** — GRO volume 11, page 329. Berkeley is in Thornbury registration district, and a death on 7 July falls in that quarter. She died under her married surname, which is itself evidence that a Saniger marriage happened.

The **1851 census** gives her birthplace, in the enumerator's own spelling, as **«Wooton under Edge»**, and her age as **81**. Her baptism is not in England Births & Baptisms — **no Lydia Jones at all is baptised in Gloucestershire between 1765 and 1775, against 939 Jones baptisms in the county in those eleven years** — but the place and the year do not need it. They are on a record she was alive to answer.
Married John Saniger at Berkeley in 1797

There **is** a Lydia marrying a John at Berkeley in that window, and she is the only one in twenty-one years: **LYDIA JONES, 8 January 1798**. Her husband's surname, in the transcript rather than in the result row, is **SAWYER**. Berkeley has **272 marriages indexed for 1793-1803**, so the parish is covered, and no Saniger marries there in that decade under any of eight spellings.
Her parents were William Jones and Sarah

It rests entirely on the maiden name, and the maiden name rests entirely on the marriage that turned out to be a Sawyer's. **JONES is now disputed rather than untested.** Wotton-under-Edge survives; Jones does not.
lydiaTested.where: A Lydia marrying a John at Berkeley in 1798, one year out from the date the tree gives and in the right parish, is a very close match on everything a result row displays — **first name, spouse's first name, place, year**. The only field that rules it out is the spouse's surname, and that field is not in the result row. It is one click further in, on the transcript. The likeliest account of «Lydia Jones» is that somebody stopped one click early, twenty years ago, and every tree since has copied it.
lydiaTested.fit: The 1841 census has a seventy-year-old **Lyddya Sinegar** in Hannah's house in Bristol. The 1851 census has **Lydia Sanigar, 81, born Wotton-under-Edge**, back at Ham in Berkeley. The GRO registers her death there months later. **Lydia is real, she is a Saniger by marriage, her age is right in three records and her birthplace is on one of them.** It is her maiden name and her wedding that were invented.

ham.head: Clapton, in the village of Ham
ham.lede: Following Lydia into the census does something the baptism registers could not: it puts this family at **an address**. Both censuses place them in **Ham**, one of the three hamlets of Berkeley parish that the 1608 muster names — and the manor whose court roll of 1587 sits in John Smyth's own collection, MS 3549, as **«Ham and Hinton»**. The family this archive has been tracing through spellings turns out to have been living, in living memory, in the place the archive has been reading fourteenth-century deeds about.
ham.c1: HO107/347, book 6, folio 3, page 1, schedule 761. Ages of adults are rounded down to the nearest five in 1841, so «35» covers a man of 37.
ham.c2: HO107/1957, folio 561, page 13, schedule 46, Berkeley sub-district.
ham.twinsHead: The twins, and why the index looked wrong
ham.twins: The complete baptism sweep found **two Berkeley baptisms in 1835 to a father John — a John and a William** — and read as index entries alone that looks like the duplication this set is full of. It is not. The 1841 census has **William 6 and John 6 in the same household**. They are twins, and the two baptisms are two children.
ham.whoHead: Who the head of that house was
ham.who: Lydia is **mother-in-law** to the widowed Ann of 1851, so Ann's late husband was Lydia's son. The children William and Mary Ann were both **baptised at Berkeley naming a father JOHN** — William and John in 1835, Mary Ann in 1838. A **John Sanigar's death is registered in the Thornbury district in the first quarter of 1850**, which is why Ann is a widow in the March of 1851. The John Saniger baptised at Berkeley on 18 September 1803, Hannah's brother, was 46 in 1850. **Everything fits and nothing yet proves it**: the identification rests on a first name, a parish and an age, and the death certificate has not been ordered.
ham.thenHead: And what it does to the medieval work
ham.then: This archive has spent a fortnight on **Swonhungre**, the fourteenth-century form of the name, and on the hamlet of **Saniger** in Berkeley that the surname came from. It had no evidence that the modern family was still anywhere near it. Now it has two censuses putting them at **Clapton in Ham**, which is the next hamlet, in the same parish, in the same manor. **That is proximity, not descent** — no document joins the 1841 household to the 1390 wardship deed, and this archive has already invented one family out of thin air this month. But it is the first time the two halves of the work have been in the same field.

lydiaHunt.head: Where Lydia did not marry
lydiaHunt.lede: JONES was disputed on 16 September, when the marriage the whole internet cites turned out to belong to a **Sawyer**. That left a question rather than an answer: **where did John Saniger marry, and to whom?** Three days of the obvious tests have not found it, and the shape of the failure is now worth as much as a find would have been.
steps: Her household's transcript identifiers run in sequence, so the street can be walked either side of her door. **Samuel and Mary Ann Nelmes and their baby** on one side; **Stephen Smith, farmer, 57, born Berkeley**, his wife Sarah and three servants on the other. No relative of Lydia's is named in either, and there is no Jones in the village.

She was born at Wotton-under-Edge, and a bride usually married at home. **One Lydia marries a «Jno.» at Wotton-under-Edge in the whole window** — Lydia Howell, 2 April 1794. The result row shows the groom's forename and stops there. The transcript gives his surname: **COSSENS**.

**No SANIGER, SANIGAR, SAINGER, SANIGOR, SANEGAR, SINEGAR, SINNEGAR or SANNIGER marries anywhere in England between 1790 and 1802** in England Marriages 1538-1973. The last before the gap is John Saniger to Elizabeth at Thornbury in 1790; the next after it is William Saniger to Mary at Thornbury in 1803.
lydiaHunt.ctlHead: And the controls hold, which is what makes this worth publishing
lydiaHunt.ctl: A null about a parish is worthless unless the parish is in the book. **Berkeley has 272 marriages indexed for 1793-1803. Wotton-under-Edge has ten full pages of them for 1792-1802**, and not one carries any spelling of this surname. Both of the two parishes where this marriage should be are well covered, and it is in neither.
lydiaHunt.means: Four readings, and this archive cannot yet choose between them. They married **somewhere else** — a licence could take them to any parish in the diocese. They married in a register **this transcription does not include**, which is an ordinary gap and not a mystery. The entry exists but is **indexed under a spelling not yet tried** — nine have been, and the surname has run to at least fifteen. Or **they did not marry at all**, which the archive raises because a woman keeping the surname and dying under it does not by itself prove a wedding.
lydiaHunt.next: **The Berkeley marriage register itself, 1795 to 1799, read by eye rather than through an index** — the same answer the RCB Library gave about Wicklow, and for the same reason. Failing that, the Gloucester diocesan **marriage licence bonds and allegations**, which survive separately from the registers and would name both parties, their parishes and often her father.
